$comment: Accepted dependency-vulnerability risk, read by `pnpm audit:deps`
(tools/audit-dependencies.ts, LINK-urjaxlrz). Entries here SUPPRESS a high or
critical advisory; nothing else can, and `pnpm audit --ignore` is never used
because it records no reason and no expiry.
Each entry requires: `advisory` (GHSA id), `module` (asserted against the
advisory's own package name — a mismatch fails rather than suppresses),
`reason` (at least 20 characters of actual reasoning), `acceptedOn` and
`reviewBy` is inclusive: ON that date the exception stops suppressing and the
advisory blocks again. That is the point — an accepted risk expires instead of
becoming permanent by being forgotten. Extending one is a deliberate edit with
a fresh reason, not a bump.
An entry matching no advisory in the current report is printed as stale and
should be deleted; it does not fail the command, because a dependency being
fixed upstream is good news, not a build break.
The list is empty on purpose. Accepting a known-vulnerable dependency is a
maintainer decision; the mechanism ships without any such decision pre-made.
